senses.gloss: m. (עִרְעֵר I) protest; evidence of illegitimacy or disqualification.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 21b:10">Keth. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>וקרא ע׳ על אחד מהן</he> and the qualification of one of the judges was contested; <cite ref="Ketubot 21b:10">ib.</cite> sq. <he>ע׳ דמאי</he> of what nature was that alleged disqualification?; <he>ע׳ דגזלנותא</he> a disqualification based on the charge of robbery; <he>ע׳ דפגם משפחה</he> based on alleged family blemish (descent from slaves).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 31b:11">B. Bath. 31ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>ע׳ חד איכא וכ׳</he> they differ as to acting on the evidence of disqualification proffered by one witness; <he>ר׳ אלעזר סבר ע׳ חד</he> R. El. is of the opinion that evidence of disqualification by one witness is sufficient; <he>ע׳ תרי</he> it requires two witnesses; <cite ref="Ketubot 26a:9">Keth. 26ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 26a:9">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>אין ע׳ פחות משנים</he> in charges of disqualification no less than two witnesses are required.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 1:5:4">Y. Bicc. I, 64ᵃ</cite> <he>משפחה … שהיו קורין עליה ע׳</he> a family … whose qualification for marriage with priests was disputed; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 8:2:12">Y. Yeb. VIII, 9ᵇ</cite> bot.; Bab.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:3:3">Y. Keth. II, 26ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>שטר שנקרא עליו ע׳</he> a document against which an informality was charged; a. fr.
